A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MixReasoning and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial methodological revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and token-use results on three mathematics benchmarks, budget sweeps, layerwise LoRA ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, controller and training-data ablations, switching behavior, and latency measurements. Its appendices add coding, commonsense, and Pass@k results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces single-token normalized entropy and backward/forward regeneration windows with sliding-window averages of negative top-k log-probabilities. v2 also introduces a minimum dwell time and one-window rollback. These substantially change the switching procedure, while retaining the LoRA-based mode-control framework and training objective.

E1.justification: The three mathematics evaluation benchmarks remain, while v2 adds GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench, StrategyQA, and CommonsenseQA, extending evaluation to science, executable code, and commonsense reasoning. Default adapter training moves from GSM8K to DeepScaleR-40K; GSM8K remains in a training-data comparison that also includes OpenMathReasoning-300K.

E2.justification: v2 adds fixed concise-mode controls, O1-Pruner, and Thinkless. Its named-method comparison uses BeConcise (Renze and Guven) instead of v1's Prompt baseline (Han et al.), removes ConciseHint, and retains CoT-Valve, DEER, and NoWait. Unlike v1's comparisons across multiple backbones, the expanded named-baseline panel is reported only for Qwen3-8B.

E3.justification: The main evaluation adds DeepSeek-R1-7B and replaces QwQ-32B-Preview with QwQ-32B. Training changes from up to ten epochs to one, with LoRA rank/scaling changing from 2/8 to 32/64. v2 specifies a uniform 16,384-token cap and adds Pass@2–5 evaluation, controller controls, and measured latency protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit threshold/window ablations, random/reverse/keyword switching controls, alternative distribution-based signals, training-data comparisons, switching statistics, and latency analysis. v1's layerwise LoRA study and three-model budget-sweep plots are removed. The house-flipping case is retained in Appendix D, while other qualitative examples are replaced.

E5.justification: Five-independent-run averaging is retained; no increased run count is established. v2 adds small capped error bars to the latency plot in Figure 6, but does not define their statistical meaning. Accuracy tables continue to report means without uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main numerical results are extensively replaced, and new benchmark, ablation, latency, and Pass@k results are added. For example, the Qwen3-8B/AIME24 MixReasoning entry changes from 64.33% and 10,738 tokens in v1 to 67.33% and 8,873 tokens in v2. These are results under revised methods and training, not controlled same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Beyond revised controller definitions, v2 adds Proposition C.1 and a proof characterizing confidence through reverse KL and establishing monotonicity under majorization at fixed top-k probability mass. Appendices C.2–C.3 add mathematical comparisons with alternative signals and an assumption-dependent switching-overhead bound; v1 has no corresponding proofs.

C1.justification: v2 makes robust sliding-window difficulty estimation and its claimed correspondence with human problem-solving explicit central contributions, extending v1's entropy-triggered compression framing. It also broadens and quantifies the headline efficiency claim to 13%–49% token reductions across mathematics and GPQA. The overarching intra-response adaptive-reasoning claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 introduces interpretations concerning transferable thresholds, the benefits of segment-level confidence, difficulty-dependent switching, and the limited benefits of scaling concise-training data. It removes v1's interpretation that reasoning-length control resides primarily in MLPs. The explicit limitations concerning calibration, non-local dependencies, and an unlearned controller are also removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, prompt templates, decoding settings, vLLM serving information, SFTTrainer/DeepSpeed details, and a code-access link. Appendix B documents selecting the shortest correct response from ten teacher samples and changes reported hardware from four A100s to four H100s. Conversely, v1's explicit flexible-match answer-extraction rule is no longer documented.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through dual-process cognition, confidence-based inference including DeepConf, and formal uncertainty measures. It also adds literature supporting the new datasets and serving implementation, while removing the earlier MLP-memory positioning and associated references. The broad distinctions from compression, hybrid reasoning, and speculation remain.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around fast/slow reasoning and explicit contributions, and the method is reorganized around how and when to switch. Experiments are restructured into main results, baseline comparisons, ablations, and further analysis. The appendix is reorganized into algorithm, implementation, theoretical/empirical analysis, and qualitative-example sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text to a two-column layout, restructures the main results into separate fixed-mode and named-baseline tables, and revises the controller schematic. It adds confidence visualizations, ablation displays, latency plots, and appendix tables. The retained house-flipping figure moves to the appendix, while the earlier budget-sweep and layerwise figures disappear.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidence gaps in v1 through direct switching-control comparisons, measured end-to-end latency, and evaluation beyond mathematics. Algorithm 1, the detailed training recipe, and the confidence-score proof substantially improve assessability and reproducibility. Removing explicit limitations and leaving accuracy uncertainty unquantified are drawbacks, but the stronger validation of the mechanism and practical efficiency provides a substantial net improvement.
